feedback: D1 is excellent. You catalogued all ten of the real findings (and a few defensible extras) with the correct OWASP class, a CWE, and a quoted code or log line for each: the SQLi concat at A03/CWE-89, unsalted MD5 at A02 (CWE-328 is fine even though the key uses 916), alg:none at A07, the hardcoded sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 secret at CWE-798, missing exp at CWE-613, the stored XSS beacon at 02:18:47, the XXE SYSTEM entity, path traversal at 02:24:02, open redirect, and the cookie flags. Your decoy verdict is right: you named the b64url helpers and proved they are pure format conversion rather than a trust decision, and you correctly kept alg:none in your findings as a live bug rather than calling it the decoy. The only thing that would have earned the last point is proving the safe construct at the mechanism level, naming the HS256 verify branch and explaining that hash_equals is constant-time, so I held D1 at 29. D2 is solid but thinner. Your PoC strings are verbatim and your CVSS vectors carry justification sentences, which is what earns credit, but two things cost you: your SQLi vector uses A:H when the auth bypass does not touch availability, so it should be A:N for about 9.1, and your customer-data vector stays S:U when the forged super_admin token reaches the shared /api/v1/internal service, which is a genuine scope change to S:C and the senior insight the exercise is testing. Your chain is also missing three hops that are in the capture, the 02:14:08 recon, the 02:14:55 failed guess, and the 02:21:13 open redirect, and presenting exfil before file read scrambles the real timeline. Your impact work is good and honest, 312 customers, the 6,400 to 950,000 naira range, and an explicit note that the full total cannot be derived from the redacted sample, though stating the tens-of-millions aggregate with that assumption would have been stronger. D3 is the highlight. The executive summary is jargon-free and lands on customers and naira, the threat model is clear, the decoy is restated correctly, and crucially you ordered remediation by effort to risk rather than CVSS, with an effort column and a rationale, which many candidates get wrong. Your two detection stopgaps name exact fields and regex for the login.php SQLi and the jwt.header.alg=none check, so the only gap is giving a qualitative false-positive read of Low and Very low instead of an estimated rate, which held that row a point short, and the report condenses to six findings rather than carrying all ten through. D4 answers all four prompts in your own voice, cites ISC2 Canons I and II by number, and ties NDPA 2023 Section 40 and the 72-hour NDPC duty to the 312 affected records; adding Section 41 on notifying the data subjects on high risk would round it out. Nothing here is fabricated; every evidence line traces to the pack. The single most important fix is your CVSS rigour in D2: drop A:H to A:N on the SQLi for about 9.1 and set S:C on the customer-data finding because the forged token crosses into the shared /api/v1/internal service.
